taxonomy_note: evidence_level uses project taxonomy CONFIRMED/STRONGLY_SUPPORTED/PLAUSIBLE/UNVERIFIED/REJECTED; claim_resolution uses CONDITIONAL/NOT_ESTABLISHED/REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE; run_status separate.

claims.statement: The admitted window (0x006C3640-0x006C3678, 23 rows) is the PREFIX of one logical function body starting at 0x006C3640 (preceded by RET 0xc at 006c363c of the previous body; body continues beyond 0x006C3678). The window loads four stack arguments into registers via fixed ESP-offset reads after each PUSH: stack_arg[1]->EDI, stack_arg[2]->EBP, stack_arg[3]->ESI, stack_arg[4]->EBX (stack_arg[k] = DWORD at [ESP_entry+4+4k]); stack_arg[0] is never read in-window; entry ECX is never used before being overwritten at 006c3658.
evidence: EXTRACT rows 006c3640-006c3654: PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,[ESP+0x10]; PUSH EDI; MOV EDI,[ESP+0x10]; PUSH EBX; MOV EBX,[ESP+0x20]; PUSH ESI; MOV ESI,[ESP+0x20] with ESP bookkeeping: after 1/2/3/4 pushes the offsets resolve to entry slots [E0+0x0C],[E0+0x08],[E0+0x14],[E0+0x10] = stack_arg[2],[1],[4],[3]
premises: ESP-offset arithmetic assumes standard x86 push semantics (no implicit ESP manipulation in-window) - CONFIRMED by rows
Role labels (which arg is begin/end/queue/callback) are ARG-SHAPE INFERENCE, established by downstream usage (C2/C3), not by the loads themselves
Calling-convention class (cdecl vs thiscall) and total stack-arg count NOT determinable in-window: epilogue/RET is out-of-window
claims.countermodel: If this were thiscall with ECX=unused this, the stack slots would still be read identically; no in-window row distinguishes. If an out-of-window prologue existed before 006c3640, PUSH EBP at 006c3640 would be mid-body - REFUTED in-window by the preceding RET 0xc at 006c363c (adjacent-row boundary check, disclosed in NAVIGATION_CENSUS N5).
claims.condition: mechanical loads CONFIRMED; role labels conditional on usage claims P09-C2/P09-C3

claims.statement: ENQUEUE SEMANTICS (core answer): the body iterates over an element range [stack_arg[1], stack_arg[2]) held in EDI..EBP (exit when EDI==EBP, checked at entry via CMP/JZ to out-of-window 0x006C369C). Per iteration it (a) calls the indirect callback in EBX with ECX = current element (MOV ECX,EDI; CALL EBX), (b) takes the callback's EAX result as a pointer to a 2-DWORD payload pair and, at the queue write-cursor ECX=[ESI+4], stores the pair as one 8-byte entry ([ECX]<-[EAX]; [ECX+4]<-[EAX+4]), then (c) advances the cursor by one entry: [ESI+4] += 8. Branch structure: if [ESI+4]==[ESI+8] -> JZ out-of-window capacity-event path 0x006C3678; else if [ESI+4]==NULL -> JZ 0x006C3672 skip-store count-only advance; else full store+advance.
evidence: rows 006c365c-006c3666 (cursor load, limit compare, JZ 006c3678, TEST, JZ 006c3672)
NAVIGATION_CENSUS N4: back-edge 006c368f JNZ 0x006c3658 exists (loop head is in-window row 006c3658)
premises: ARG-SHAPE INFERENCE (labeled): EDI/EBP = element range begin/end - supported by entry equality check and loop re-entry; element STRIDE is NOT determinable in-window (stride arithmetic is in out-of-window loop tail)
callback returns its payload-pointer in EAX (standard EAX-return premise; first iteration has no in-window EAX init, so the store path requires the callback to produce EAX)
the callback is invoked thiscall-shaped with ECX=current element (from MOV ECX,EDI immediately before CALL EBX) - ABI INFERENCE, callee body out-of-window
identical names/shapes do not prove common semantics: the 2-DWORD pair is mechanically copied; its semantic identity ({0x66,A} request) is inherited from cited P07 caller context, not proven here
claims.countermodel: If the callback clobbers ESI (callee-saved violation) or returns non-EAX, the pair store would read a wrong pointer; in-window rows cannot exclude this - callback body out-of-window. If [ESI+4] were a byte-count rather than pointer, direct dereference at 006c366a would fault; pointer interpretation is dominant but rests on code-correctness premise.
claims.condition: mechanics CONFIRMED in-window; payload semantic identity and callback behavior conditional on out-of-window/cited-P07 context

claims.statement: QUEUE OBJECT AND FIELDS WRITTEN (core answer): the queue object is stack_arg[3] (4th stack DWORD), held in ESI. In-window field census: [ESI+0x0] NEVER touched in-window (role unknown - possible head/base/other, no evidence); [ESI+0x4] is the write/tail cursor POINTER into an entry array (read at 006c365c, written ONLY at 006c3672 as +=8) - it is the ONLY queue-object field written in-window; [ESI+0x8] is a limit/end value compared for equality with the cursor (read at 006c365f, NEVER written in-window). There is NO count-field update, NO head-field update and NO entry-pointer store into the object in-window. The 'entry pointer store' of the transport is the in-place 2-DWORD payload write at the cursor target ([ECX],[ECX+4]) - entry memory, not object fields. The enqueue commits an entry purely by advancing [ESI+4] by 8.
evidence: direct dereference of ECX loaded from [ESI+4] at 006c366a/006c366f proves pointer interpretation of [+4]
premises: [+8] interpreted as end/limit pointer (or comparable bound) by equality with a proven pointer - PLAUSIBLE, its dereference never occurs in-window so pointer-ness of [+8] is weaker than [+4]
class identity of the queue object is UNKNOWN in-window (no RTTI, no names; identical shape to any append-buffer does not prove semantics)
claims.countermodel: A different object field could serve as head/count outside the window; a consumer may drain entries and repair [+4] out-of-window. The NULL-skip path degeneracy: after cursor==NULL the ADD makes [+4]=8, a non-null invalid pointer; unless the out-of-window capacity-event path at 0x006C3678 (reachable whenever [+4]==[+8], including NULL==NULL) re-establishes the buffer, a subsequent iteration with cursor=8 would fault at [ECX] - in-window rows cannot exclude that the code relies on out-of-window repair or single-element ranges in counting mode.
claims.condition: field-write census is CONFIRMED for the 23 in-window rows only; object-class identity and out-of-window field roles remain open

claims.statement: ENTRY LAYOUT (core answer): one queue entry = 8 bytes = 2 DWORDs: entry[+0x0] = payload dword0 (copied from [EAX]), entry[+0x4] = payload dword1 (copied from [EAX+4]). Entries are appended densely (cursor += 8 per entry); no per-entry header/tag/size field appears in-window.
premises: payload pointer = callback EAX result (see C2 premise)
pair semantic identity ({type,id}-shaped {0x66,A} per P07) is CITED, not proven in-window
claims.countermodel: If the callback returns a pointer to a larger record, only the first 8 bytes are transported here; no in-window evidence about payload beyond the two DWORDs.
claims.condition: layout CONFIRMED as transported pair; semantics of the two DWORDs inherited from cited P07 context

claims.statement: CANDIDATES (2, within reserve) for the out-of-window capacity-event path reached when [ESI+4]==[ESI+8] (JZ 0x006C3678): CAND-A = grow/extend-on-full (bounded linear append buffer; equal means exhausted; handler reallocates/extends, then enqueue continues); CAND-B = lazy-allocate-or-flush (equal state includes empty/unallocated buffer, e.g. NULL==NULL on first use; handler establishes or drains the buffer). Both are consistent with all in-window rows; they are NOT distinguishable in-window.
evidence: in-window: only the equality compare and the JZ exist (rows 006c365f-006c3662); the handler body at 0x006C3678 is out-of-window and NOT analyzed
premises: both candidates preserve the in-window mechanics unchanged
no preference between A/B is claimed
claims.countermodel: any third behavior (e.g., drop-on-full, error path) also fits in-window rows; the candidate set is a reserve-bounded pair, not an exhaustive proof of two
claims.condition: distinguishing evidence = out-of-window body at 0x006C3678 (and its callee), requires separate admission
